Subject: Invoice RWI-7891: settlement currency choice + routing / intermediary fee guidance

Hi Marta / Oliver,

Please find attached Invoice RWI-20260623-7891 for the May usage period. Two quick notes on settlement:

- We can accept payment in USD (preferred) or EUR. If you choose EUR, please confirm you want us to invoice and settle in EUR — our bank will convert USD receipts to EUR internally and your bank or intermediary may apply FX.
- Wire instructions are below; the receiving bank is our USD collection account. If you pay EUR, you may be routed via an intermediary correspondent bank which can add fees.

Receiving bank (USD):
- Bank: FirstGate Bank
- Account name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Account #: 987654321
- SWIFT: FGBBUS33
- Routing / ABA (US): 122000058

Correspondent / intermediary (possible for EUR payments):
- Intermediary bank: EuroConnect S.A.
- SWIFT: ECBREU2L
- Note: If your treasury instructs a EUR payment, the intermediary may debit an intermediary fee for processing the cross-currency transfer. These fees are typically borne by the payer unless otherwise agreed.

If you'd like us to absorb a single intermediary fee this month to accelerate collection, let us know and I will route to Rafael for approval. Otherwise please instruct your bank to send "OUR" charges (payer pays all fees) so we receive the full invoice amount net.

Attached: Invoice_RWI-20260623-7891.pdf (invoice), wire_instructions_template.csv (CSV for treasury).

Thanks — please confirm preferred currency and whether your bank can send as OUR.

Best,
Laura

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <accounts@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@nimbusretail.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice RWI-7891: settlement currency choice + routing / intermediary fee guidance

Hi Marta / Oliver,

Thanks — quick clarifications to make treasury's life easier:

1) EUR IBAN: We do not currently maintain an active EUR IBAN under the Redwood collection account in the EU. If you pay EUR from Frankfurt, your bank will typically route through a correspondent (EuroConnect or similar) into our USD account and an FX conversion will happen.

2) Fee handling: Our standard policy is that the payer covers intermediary / correspondent fees (i.e., instruct as OUR). We recognize that some banks default to SHA (shared) and that results in the amount we receive being less. If you must pay SHA, please confirm and we will either (a) issue a short proforma showing the expected net received and ask you to top-up, or (b) we can absorb a single intermediary fee this month on a one-off basis if you provide a note confirming that for procurement/audit. Rafael — can you confirm whether finance can approve absorption of one intermediary fee up to EUR 35 for this invoice?

3) Alternate options:
- If Nimbus prefers to avoid FX entirely, you can pay in USD from your bank by ordering the transaction in USD (our ABA/SWIFT above). That avoids an additional intermediary leg on the EUR side.
- Another option is to use a virtual FX provider (Wise, Revolut) to create a USD transfer to our account; those providers often show lower intermediary markups.

Let me know how you'd like to proceed — if you confirm SHA, we'll have finance prepare a net-proforma and I can follow up with a request for the short top-up.

Best,
Laura
